title: Chào
summary: A relaxed hello once the moment already feels clear.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Chào is the plain greeting inside Xin chào. Use it when the moment is relaxed, the other person already feels socially clear, or you are adding a relationship word such as anh, chị, em, cô, or chú. If you are unsure, keep Xin chào as the safer first move.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Say Chào when a simple hi is enough. It is short and friendly, but it relies more on context than Xin chào.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: This is one word, but it becomes more useful when you notice what can come after it.

sections.title: Natural variations
sections.body: These are the main ways Chào becomes more specific.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use Chào with people you already know, casual service moments where the mood is friendly, or as the base before a relationship word. Use Xin chào when you are entering a new shop, approaching a desk, or unsure how formal to be.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Chào is not rude by itself; it is just lighter. Vietnamese often adds warmth through the word after Chào, so learning the relationship forms matters more than forcing one greeting everywhere.
